content.comment_body: I use [url] (Personal Software Inspector) which warns me when outdated or insecure software versions are present on my computer. [product_name] version 4 installed a copy of Java JRE [version_no] in its own directory, and after upgrading to [product_name] version 6, it created a folder with Java v6.0.10.6. The security tool flags both of those Java versions as unsafe. Can I safely delete the [product_name] directory trees containing these old Java versions, or does [product_name] need them for proper operation? My system-wide Java JRE is up to date (v6.0.150).

Dear [user_name], many forum members work daily with [product_name] in various versions. From their experiences, it doesn't appear to be insecure. Since [product_name] relies on Java, removing its Java environment would likely prevent it from working. I haven't used your mentioned security tool, so I can't advise on that. Personally, I've used Java and [product_name] since version 2 without encountering issues. Best regards, [user_name]

I believe you can delete the folder containing the older version of [product_name]. On my computer, several [product_name] versions were installed, and after uninstalling the older ones, folders from those versions remained with some files. The current version contains all necessary files. If something is missing, you can simply reinstall the software. Additionally, some old files persist in Documents and Settings. If you're uncertain about deleting something, you could share a screenshot of your directory structure for further assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are debating the risks of outdated Java Runtime Environments bundled with older [product_name] versions. One user reports that a security tool flags these Java directories as insecure, prompting concern about deleting them. Responses show some uncertainty but generally agree that only the latest [product_name] version's directory is needed, while older directories may be removable unless the program explicitly requires them.
analysis.user_expectations: User hopes to delete obsolete Java installations associated with previous [product_name] versions without compromising the functionality of the current software.
